news.headline: Hackers Breach U.S. Air Force Cloud One Computing Platform
news.summary: Reuters reported that hackers infiltrated the Air Force's Cloud One platform, the service that hosts many of the service's applications and data. The breach was discovered during routine maintenance and upgrades. Officials did not comment on the security posture or the amount of data accessed. The incident adds to a series of recent cyber incidents affecting U.S. government systems.

news.headline: Nebraska Sen. Deb Fischer confirms husband died by suicide after initial peaceful report
news.summary: Senator Deb Fischer's office announced that her husband, Bruce Fischer, died by suicide, correcting earlier statements that he had passed away peacefully. The update was posted on social media and confirmed by multiple news outlets. The clarification highlights the family's request for understanding and privacy. The incident draws attention to mental health issues and the handling of death announcements by public officials.

news.headline: Two American Airlines jets collide on the tarmac at Reagan National Airport
news.summary: During taxi for departure on Friday evening, two American Airlines Boeing 737s made contact, with one aircraft clipping the wing of the other near Runway 19 at Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport. No injuries were reported and the Federal Aviation Administration said it will investigate the incident. The collision caused an arriving flight to abort its landing and both planes returned to their gates.

news.headline: U.S. Central Command disables commercial vessel attempting to breach Iran blockade in Gulf of Oman
news.summary: U.S. Central Command reported that a commercial ship was disabled in the Gulf of Oman after it attempted to run a U.S. naval blockade of Iranian ports. The vessel received multiple warnings before the strike. The incident highlights ongoing tensions between the United States and Iran over maritime security. It underscores the U.S. commitment to enforce its blockade policy.

news.headline: New York State Senate Majority Leader Andrea Stewart-Cousins dies at 76
news.summary: Andrea Stewart-Cousins, the Democratic leader of the New York State Senate, died on Friday at age 76. She had been reelected weeks earlier and was the first Black woman to lead the chamber. Her death was announced by Senate communications staff. The passing prompts a leadership transition for the Senate Democrats.

news.headline: Steelers bench veteran quarterback Aaron Rodgers amid coach-player clash
news.summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers announced that starting quarterback Aaron Rodgers will not play, naming Mason Rudolph as the starter for the upcoming game. Coach Mike McCarthy cited disagreements over the offense as the reason for the benching. Rodgers responded with a heated interview accusing the coach of unprofessional behavior. The move raises questions about Rodgers' future with the team and the franchise's direction.

news.headline: NBC pulls anti‑Israel ad aired during SNL Thanksgiving special after Jewish group backlash
news.summary: A 30‑second advertisement opposing U.S. military aid to Israel was broadcast during a Saturday Night Live Thanksgiving special on NBC. The ad, paid for by the Institute for Middle East Understanding, linked U.S. funding to Israel's war in Gaza. Jewish advocacy organizations and Israeli officials condemned the spot as antisemitic, prompting NBC to cease further airings. The incident highlights tensions over how the Israel‑Gaza conflict is presented in U.S. media.

news.headline: California law mandates booster seats for children up to age 16 with safety test option
news.summary: California has enacted a law that, starting January 1, 2027, requires children up to age 16 to use a booster seat unless they pass a five‑point safety test. The bill, authored by Assemblymember Lori Wilson, applies to minors ages 8 to 15 and includes penalties for non‑compliance. The measure aims to improve child passenger safety by ensuring proper seat belt fit. It will affect parents, drivers, and teen passengers statewide.

news.headline: Donald Trump Jr. condemns Netflix for posting lesbian scene on Thanksgiving
news.summary: On Thanksgiving, Netflix shared a 16‑second clip from the series "The Hunting Wives" that shows two female characters kissing. Donald Trump Jr. posted a criticism of the clip on X, questioning the platform's decision. The post sparked a wave of reactions across the political spectrum. The incident highlights ongoing cultural disputes over media content and platform responsibility.

news.headline: Mexico's President Sheinbaum condemns U.S. DEA tip line as foreign interference
news.summary: Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum criticized the U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration for creating an anonymous tip line that allows reports on cartel activity and corrupt officials in Mexico. She said the program interferes with Mexico's sovereignty and urged the DEA to focus on its own domestic issues. The DEA launched the line as part of its effort to combat drug trafficking. The dispute highlights tensions over cross‑border drug enforcement.
